title: Coefficient Identification in Confounded Linear Models with Chordless Feedback Cycles
banked_reason: D0.5 graded the sound exact fiber theorem subfield: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < field gate 7.4, salvageable=false; broader coupled-swap or operational recovery work is a new program.
gap_reasons: The restricted graph scope, lack of a general coupled-swap classification, and absence of a law-to-parameter implementation keep the package below flagship significance and constrain its leading-journal score.
Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded, or re-anchor the proposal (rewind D-1.2).
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved an exact generic affine-plus-reciprocal-swap fiber decomposition and a polynomial path-rank/swap target certificate, including explicit same-law alternatives and a coupled-double-swap boundary witness. F1.5 found and D0 repaired a missing declared-edge premise without changing the result; re-review then capped the sound package at subfield. Reaching field tier would require a materially new coupled-swap classification or an operational law-to-parameter recovery theory, so Lean formalization stopped before F2.
tldr: For known mixed graphs whose nontrivial directed SCCs are chordless cycles, with singleton acyclic SCCs also allowed, the full-distribution coefficient fiber is generically the union of the published removable-ancestor affine fiber and independent reciprocal swaps. A swap survives exactly on a wholly unconfounded two-cycle whose two vertices have identical external-parent sets. The only incidence restriction needed is local: no two distinct two-cycle SCCs may share two districts. Arbitrary longer SCC--district incidence cycles, and four-cycles having an SCC-side vertex of size at least three, are allowed. This normal form yields a polynomial-size max-flow and graph-scan certificate for any declared coefficient vector and explicit same-law alternatives whenever the certificate fails.
gap: The closest model-matched paper completely characterizes acyclic fibers but in cyclic graphs proves only sufficiency of the removable-ancestor equations, a necessary identification condition, and special unconfounded-cycle cases. It does not control how arbitrary nonlinear confounding constrains feedback-induced row permutations across multiple SCCs.
